newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major sticks to parliament recess date.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major sticks to parliament recess date.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday he had no intention of delaying parliament's recess, due on Friday.
"There has already been a Privy Council determining prorogation. I have no intention of changing that," he told parliament, in the last prime ministers' question time before the May 1 election.
"Prorogation always follows within days of an election announcement. When I announced it there was no representation...from the Labour Party about changing the date of the election," Major said.

The opposition Labour and Liberal parties have demanded parliament stays open beyond this week to allow publication of a report into sleaze allegations against 10 ruling party members. An interim report published on Thursday cleared 15 MPs of any wrongdoing but left a question mark hanging over another 10.
Labour leader Tony Blair said there was no reason why the report could not be published before the May 1 election that Labour is strongly tipped to win.
But Major refused, accusing Labour and the Liberal Democrats of a "political stunt" designed to draw attention away from an excellent set of economic figures.
